stem.text: A particle moves in the xy-plane so that its position at time t is \( \left(x(t), y(t)\right) = \left( - t^{2} + 3 \sin{\left(t \right)} - 8,\ - \frac{t^{3}}{3} + t \right) \) for \( 0 \le t \le \frac{5}{2} \). For \( 0 \le t \le \frac{5}{2} \), \( x(t) < 0 \). Using a calculator where needed, find all times t in the open interval \( 0 < t < \frac{5}{2} \) at which the particle is moving toward the y-axis. Give a reason for your answer, and give any decimal endpoint correct to three decimal places.

answer_key.label: The particle moves toward the y-axis for \( 0 < t < 0.915 \), because \( x(t) \) and \( x'(t) \) have opposite signs there.

worked_solution.text: The stem gives \( x(t) < 0 \) on the whole interval, so the particle stays on one side of the y-axis.

The particle moves toward the y-axis when \( x(t) \) and \( x'(t) \) have opposite signs, that is, when \( x'(t) = - 2 t + 3 \cos{\left(t \right)} > 0 \). A calculator gives \( x'(t) = 0 \) at \( t \approx 0.915 \), with \( x'(t) \) positive before that time and the opposite sign after it.
So the particle moves toward the y-axis for \( 0 < t < 0.915 \), because there \( x(t) < 0 \) and \( x'(t) > 0 \), so its distance from the y-axis, \( |x(t)| \), is decreasing.
worked_solution.rule_named: sign analysis of the velocity component

options.label: The particle moves toward the y-axis for \( 0 < t < \frac{5}{2} \), because \( x(t) \) is negative there.
options.derivation: the sign of the coordinate read as the direction of motion, so every time with x(t) < 0 counted as approaching

options.label: The particle moves toward the y-axis for \( 0.915 < t < \frac{5}{2} \), because \( x'(t) \) is negative there.
options.derivation: approaching read as a negative rate, so the times with x'(t) < 0 taken without the sign of x(t)

options.label: The particle moves toward the y-axis for \( 0 < t < 1 \), because \( y'(t) \) is positive there.
options.derivation: the other velocity component used, so the times with y'(t) > 0 reported
